'''Yves André''' (born December 11, 1959) is a French mathematician, specializing in [[arithmetic geometry]].

==Biography==
André received his doctorate in 1984 from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris VI) with thesis advisor Daniel Bertrand and thesis ''Structure de Hodge, équations différentielles p-adiques, et indépendance algébrique de périodes d'intégrales abéliennes''.<ref>{{Mathgenealogy|id=63434}}</ref> He became at [[CNRS]] in 1985 a Researcher, in 2000 a Research Director 2nd Class, and in 2009 a Research Director 1st Class (at [[École Normale Supérieure]] and [[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=Yves André|website=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/André_Yves}}</ref>

==Research==
In 1989, he formulated the one-dimensional-subvariety case of what is now known as the [[André-Oort conjecture]] on special subvarieties of Shimura varieties.<ref>"G-functions and geometry", Vieweg 1989</ref> Only partial results have been proven so far; by André himself and by [[Jonathan Pila]] in 2009. In 2016, André used [[Peter Scholze|Scholze]]'s method of [[perfectoid space]]s to prove [[Melvin Hochster]]'s direct summand conjecture that any finite extension of a regular [[commutative ring]] splits as a module.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=André, Yves|title=La conjecture du facteur direct|year=2016|eprint=1609.00345|class=math.AG}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Bhatt, Bhargav|author-link=Bhargav Bhatt (mathematician)|title=On the direct summand conjecture and its derived variant|eprint=1608.08882|year=2016|class=math.AG}}.</ref>

==Awards==
In 2011, André received the [[Prix Paul Doistau–Émile Blutet]] of the [[Académie des Sciences]]. In 2015, he was elected as a [[Member of the Academia Europaea]]. He was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]] and gave a talk titled ''Perfectoid spaces and the homological conjectures''.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=André, Yves|title=Perfectoid spaces and the homological conjectures|eprint=1801.10006|year=2018|class=math.AC}}</ref>
